# Results — Study 396 (Reshoring-Basket)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The **reshoring / nearshoring
trade** — US industrials (`XLI`) + Mexico (`EWW`) + factory automation (`ROK`), equal weight
— tested as a persistent thematic tilt against two benchmarks (US `SPY`, global `ACWI`). The
question is **not** "did the basket go up" (almost everything did) but "did it out-earn its
benchmark by more than its **beta** explains, robustly, net of costs?". Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — `XLI`, `EWW`, `ROK`, `SPY`, `ACWI` (public, no key) |
| Window | 1999-01-05 → 2026-06-18 (**6,906** trading days; **27.4** years) |
| Basket | equal-weight daily return of `XLI` (US industrials) / `EWW` (Mexico) / `ROK` (automation) |
| Benchmarks | `SPY` (US, full sample) and `ACWI` (global, from 2008 — the honest yardstick) |
| Cash rate | flat 2%/yr for the excess-of-cash Sharpe race |
| Entry / costs | buy-and-hold tilt; long-basket / short-benchmark book, **annual** rebalance, one-way cost × turnover |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The "reshoring trade" has no canonical ticker.
> Our three-sleeve equal-weight basket is a transparent **proxy** — and it carries
> **survivorship at the single-name level** (`ROK` is a name that *survived and compounded*;
> the automation sleeve is one stock, not a diversified theme). The basket is also **high
> beta** (β ≈ 1.04 vs SPY), so a naïve "excess return" overstates the edge: most of it is
> sector beta you were always paid for. We therefore lead with the **beta-adjusted CAPM
> alpha**, not the raw excess.

## The signal — raw excess vs beta-adjusted alpha (full sample)

The raw excess is the basket minus the benchmark; the **alpha** is the regression intercept
of (basket − cash) on (benchmark − cash) — the part the benchmark does *not* explain. HAC =
Newey-West (21-lag) autocorrelation-robust *t*; the desk's `REAL` bar is **HAC t ≥ 2 on the
alpha**.

| benchmark | excess /yr | plain *t* | HAC *t* (excess) | **alpha /yr** | β | **HAC *t* (alpha)** | Sharpe basket | Sharpe bench |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY** (US) | **+4.93%** | 1.98 | **2.07** | **+4.60%** | 1.04 | **1.93** | 0.55 | 0.42 |
| **ACWI** (global, 2008+) | +3.15% | — | 1.24 | **+2.51%** | 1.08 | **1.01** | 0.46 | 0.41 |

Read it carefully. Against SPY the *raw* excess just clears the HAC bar (t = 2.07) — but the
moment you **strip the beta**, the alpha is **+4.6%/yr at HAC t = 1.93 — under 2**. Against
the *proper* global benchmark `ACWI`, the alpha is a thin **+2.5%/yr at HAC t = 1.01** —
indistinguishable from zero. The basket out-Sharpes its benchmark, but by a margin a high-beta
industrials+EM tilt would deliver in any rising market. There is no robust beta-adjusted edge.

## The kill shot — the "edge" is entirely *pre*-narrative, and reverses *after*

The reshoring story is a **post-2018** narrative (the US–China tariff war + the 2020 COVID
supply-chain scare). If the trade were *driven* by reshoring, it should work *most* in that
era. It does the opposite. Split the tape at 2018-01-01 (pre-announced, not snooped):

| sub-period | n days | excess /yr | **alpha /yr** | **HAC *t* (alpha)** | β | Sharpe basket | Sharpe bench |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **pre-2018** (no narrative) | 4,779 | +7.60% | **+7.25%** | **+2.51** | 1.06 | 0.55 | 0.30 |
| **post-2018** (the narrative era) | 2,127 | −1.07% | **−0.99%** | **−0.24** | 0.99 | 0.54 | 0.71 |

The basket's alpha was real and significant (t = 2.51) **before anyone was talking about
reshoring**, and went **negative and insignificant (t = −0.24) exactly when the narrative
arrived** — and post-2018 the *benchmark* out-Sharpes the basket (0.71 vs 0.54). The story
gets the sign of its own thesis backwards: the trade died the moment it became a trade.

## It's one stock, not a theme — per-sleeve excess vs SPY

| sleeve | excess /yr | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| `XLI` (US industrials) | +1.13% | 0.67 |
| `EWW` (Mexico) | +3.37% | 0.89 |
| `ROK` (automation, single name) | **+10.29%** | **2.16** |

The two sleeves that *are* the reshoring thesis — US industrials and Mexico — carry **no**
significant excess. The basket's headline is carried almost entirely by **one automation
single-name** (`ROK`, t = 2.16), which is a survivorship pick, not a diversified theme. Drop
it and the "reshoring edge" evaporates.

## Costs barely matter — which tells you what kind of "edge" this is

| cost (one-way) | gross excess /yr | annual cost (2 legs × 1 rebal) | net excess /yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | +4.93% | 0.10% | +4.83% |
| 10 bps | +4.93% | 0.20% | +4.73% |
| 20 bps | +4.93% | 0.40% | +4.53% |

A buy-and-hold tilt has trivial turnover, so costs shave almost nothing — but that is **not**
good news. What survives costs is the **raw excess, which is mostly beta**; the *alpha* (the
part that isn't beta) was never significant (HAC t = 1.93 vs SPY, 1.01 vs ACWI) and is
*negative* in the era you'd actually deploy it. You can't charge costs against an edge that
isn't there once you net out the market.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic basket = `β·market + planted_alpha + idiosyncratic noise` (β ≈ 1.03), so the
*raw* excess is non-zero by construction (the basket is high-beta) but the **alpha** equals
the planted knob. The engine must (a) not manufacture a significant alpha from a high-beta
basket with **zero** planted alpha, and (b) light up on a large planted alpha:

| planted alpha | excess /yr | **alpha /yr** | β | **HAC *t* (alpha)** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0%/yr** (beta only) | +3.80% | +3.49% | 1.03 | **1.26** |
| **+10%/yr** | +13.88% | +13.57% | 1.03 | **4.88** |

With **no** planted alpha the test stays under t = 2 (across 20 seeds the alpha t centres on
0.4 and exceeds |t| = 2 only ~5% of the time — the correct false-positive rate), even though
the *raw* excess is a healthy +3.8%/yr of pure beta. Only a **huge** +10%/yr planted alpha
drives the alpha t to 4.9. The control proves the harness is unbiased — and that a high-beta
basket's raw excess is **not** evidence of alpha, which is the entire lesson.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The raw excess vs SPY just clears the HAC bar (t = 2.07), but the
  **beta-adjusted alpha fails it** (+4.6%/yr, HAC t = 1.93), and against the proper global
  benchmark `ACWI` the alpha is a thin +2.5%/yr at **HAC t = 1.01**. The edge is **entirely
  pre-2018** (alpha t = 2.51) and **negative in the post-2018 narrative era** (t = −0.24), and
  it is carried by **one single name** (`ROK`, t = 2.16), not the theme. Positive-but-fragile,
  benchmark- and sub-period-dependent ⇒ **WEAK**, not REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** What survives costs is **beta**, not alpha: a high-beta
  industrials + EM tilt out-returns the market for free in a rising tape. Strip the beta and
  there is no significant edge; and in the era you'd actually trade the narrative (post-2018)
  the residual is *negative* while the plain benchmark out-Sharpes the basket. There is no
  NAV-scale reshoring alpha to deploy.
- **Structural edge? — BUSTED.** The "manufacturing is coming home, so the basket structurally
  out-earns" claim is a **sector-beta + single-name + backward-looking illusion**: the
  outperformance is mostly beta, is concentrated in one stock, and **reverses sign exactly when
  the reshoring narrative arrives**. The thesis works only where it's uninformative (the market
  went up) and fails exactly where it would pay (a *distinct*, narrative-driven edge).
